hypothesis: Exactly geometry-orthogonal cross-input signal predicts public priors. Test whether feasible OD cycle updates can retain its matching benefit while keeping all three non-OD metrics at baseline, instead of following marginal recalibration.
source_feature: Mean normalized source prior projected exactly out of span+origin/destination geometry; target cross-fit ridge1 with one common five-fold assignment.
cycle: Sample 4*path_count fixed random valid four-zone rectangles per case, shared between strengths. Cycle(+1,-1,-1,+1) preserves all origin/destination margins. Require original prior-sign derivative0 and retain original orthant/nonnegative bounds, preserving prior L1 deviation. Each accepted step decreases L1 distance to the estimated direct candidate; no latent truth enters direction, bound or acceptance.
target: Direct nonnegative lambda0.05 predictions at fixed5% and25% prior mixture. Cycle starts at original baseline and uses the same cycle sequence for both strengths.
guarantee: Release-specific count rows are marginal combinations, so feasible cycles preserve counts, S_link/S_attr/S_dev within numerical precision. S_od can still worsen. Heuristic coordinate updates are not a proven global projection or optimum.
numerical_controls: Separate constructive nonzero rectangle and 20 oracle L1 monotonicity controls must pass before use. Oracle truth is confined to those numerical checks, never supplied to this estimator.
evaluation: Report all known-latent clipped scores AND unclipped true relative OD L1, all zero movement, accepted updates and constraint drift. Fresh artificial draws in adaptively chosen family; not whole-system blind or official validation.
scope: No real candidate or Kaggle upload; frozen official baseline retained.
